author: Associated Press
description:
State to execute man convicted of two counts of first-degree murder while Texas also plans to put a man to death

Florida is set Thursday to carry out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year on a man convicted of killing a pregnant woman and her husband during a home invasion, while Texas plans to put a man to death for the killing of a Houston jeweler during a $3.6m diamond heist.

Thomas Mitchell Overton, 71, was scheduled to receive a three-drug injection at 6pm at Florida state prison in Raiford. Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was set to receive a lethal injection about an hour later at a prison in Texas and become the ninth person executed by that state this year. The planned executions of the two septuagenarians in one day reflect the ageing of the US death row population.

Continue reading...
title: Florida to carry out record-breaking 20th execution of the year

author: Associated Press
description:
• Rose pleaded guilty to tax evasion in 1990

  • Player also banned from baseball over bets

Donald Trump says he has posthumously pardoned Pete Rose more than two years after the baseball star’s death and a year after he was reinstated by Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred.

“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR + LEGEND,” Trump posted on social media.

Continue reading...
title: Donald Trump issues posthumous pardon to MLB ‘superstar and legend’ Pete Rose

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Xavier Taylor had been hospitalized since May

  • MLB players showed support during his hospitalization

A 12-year-old New Jersey boy who was hospitalized for months after being struck by a baseball during a Little League game has died, according to announcements on social media on Wednesday night.

Xavier Taylor was warming up before a game on 26 May when he was accidentally struck on the head and collapsed on the field, according to various media reports. He was airlifted to a local hospital and was placed on a ventilator in critical condition.

Continue reading...
title: 12-year-old Little League player dies after being struck by baseball during game

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Sparks were bought for $10m in 2014

  • Walter has been selling off a number of assets

  • Chelsea owner Jose E Feliciano to buy team

Mark Walter, who has a controlling stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers, ⁠is set to sell off another sports asset, with Sportico reporting on Thursday that he is ⁠close to a deal ⁠to ​offload the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks for $750m.

San Diego Padres owners José E Feliciano ⁠and his wife, Kwanza Jones, are reportedly set to purchase the Sparks in a record deal for ⁠a WNBA team. The previous largest price came ‌when the Connecticut ‌Sun were sold for $300m in March. ‌The Sun plan to move to Houston.

Continue reading...
title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter set to sell Los Angeles Sparks for WNBA record $750m

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world

Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived.

GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.

Continue reading...
title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• Dane was sacked by Tottenham in February

  • ‘I know what I want and the direction we should go in’

Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over as manager.

The Dane was confirmed as Pierre Sage’s successor on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank admitted he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by Tottenham in February.
title: Thomas Frank admits he has a point to prove after taking reins at Crystal Palace

author: Edward Helmore and agency
description:
Trump alleges defamation by three Times reporters and Penguin Random House in campaign against news outlets

A federal ⁠judge in Florida on Thursday said Donald Trump’s $15bn defamation lawsuit against the New York Times and book publisher Penguin Random House may proceed, a victory ⁠for the US president in his ⁠legal campaign ​against media companies he accuses of treating him unfairly.

US district judge Steven Merryday in Tampa dismissed two claims in the suit while allowing core defamation claims to move forward.

Continue reading...
title: US ⁠judge allows Trump’s $15bn lawsuit against New York Times to proceed

author: Robyn Vinter North of England correspondent
description:
Politicians call attack on independent councillor Ibrar Ali canvassing in Bradford Moor ward ‘deeply disturbing’

Politicians have described an attack on a councillor who was canvassing in Bradford as “horrific” and “deeply disturbing”, after a man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

A 32-year-old man is in custody suspected of attacking Ibrar Ali at about 11am on Thursday as the independent councillor was door-knocking in his Bradford Moor ward, leaving him with a stab wound in the leg.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested after ‘horrific’ knife attack on Bradford councillor

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
David Fincher directs Quentin Tarantino’s script, picking up from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, and its lead is more ineffably beguiling than ever

We got through to the very end of Quentin Tarantino’s previous film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood without finding out exactly how, why or if Brad Pitt’s stuntman character Cliff Booth murdered his wife. It was an issue only addressed in Tarantino’s novel based on the movie. And throughout the 140 minutes of this outrageous sugar-rush sequel – scripted by Tarantino and directed by David Fincher – this subject is tactfully passed over in silence, the one point that damages our perception of Cliff’s amiable-cowpoke good nature.

Cliff is the guy who climaxed the previous picture by helping with a dramatic rescue; after, that is, gallantly refusing an age-gap relationship with Margaret Qualley’s jailbait teen. Well, we may not get the complete picture of Cliff’s matrimonial circumstances until Tarantino’s forthcoming crossover C
title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth review – Tarantino and Fincher join forces for Brad Pitt’s glorious return

author: Fiona Harvey, Graham Readfearn, Damien Gayle and Gabrielle Canon in Antalya, and Oliver Milman in New York
description:
Draft agreement also fails to show how developing countries will receive financial help to deal with climate crisis

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

Every mention of “fossil fuels” has been expunged from the draft outcome of global climate talks, which were approaching their final hours on Thursday night, threatening to turn the UN summit into what campaigners called a “ghost Cop”.

The second draft of the key text, released on Thursday afternoon and setting out the main commitments from the
title: Cop31 risks becoming ‘ghost’ summit after all mentions of ‘fossil fuels’ removed from draft text

author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague
description:
Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world

There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.

For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.
title: ‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling

author: Guardian staff
description:
Late-night hosts discussed Trump’s friendly meeting with the Russian and Chinese leaders at the Apec summit

Late-night hosts mocked Donald Trump’s friendly meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping as well as the administration’s muddled response to various tech outages.

Continue reading...
title: Jimmy Kimmel on Trump’s meeting with Xi and Putin: ‘I guess Darth Vader couldn’t make it’

author: Barry Glendenning
description:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world”, football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat.

When I first saw t
title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda

It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”.

But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “new page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century.

Continue reading...
title: New page in history? Xi, Trump and Putin summit was more of a footnote

author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv and Jakub Krupa in London
description:
Russian president makes remarks after Ukraine strikes strategic bridge to Crimea for third time in a week

Vladimir Putin has said Russia’s response to the bombing of the Kerch bridge to Crimea will be “painful”, after Ukraine attacked the strategic connection for the third time this week.

The warning was delivered at a press conference after Putin met Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China. The Russian president claimed he had been considering agreeing to local ceasefires until the Kerch road bridge was destroyed.

Continue reading...
title: Putin vows ‘painful’ response to Ukraine’s bombing of Kerch bridge

author: Fiona Sturges
description:
The author explores the life and legacy of his estranged father, from adoption and abandonment to his horrific experiences of the second world war

When Haruki Murakami was a child living in Nishinomiya, Japan, his father announced they were getting rid of their cat. He put his son and the cat on his bike and cycled along the Shukugawa river to a beach 2km from their house. There, they put the box with the cat in it on the ground among some trees and cycled away “without a backward glance”. When they got home, they opened their door to find the cat they’d just left “greeting us with a friendly meow, its tail standing tall. It had beaten us home.”

Murakami always wondered how the cat got home so quickly, and why his father had wanted to banish her. These are just some of the unanswered questions that surface in Abandoning a Cat, an essay that first appeared in the New Yorker in 2019, and which is now being published as a book and audiobook. Transl
title: Abandoning a Cat by Haruki Murakami review – an intimate meditation on family and memory

author: Gerard Meagher
description:
• Borthwick hails cavalry for Nations Championship match

  • Kiwis make eight changes after shock Wales reverse

Steve Borthwick has called on the cavalry with George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson all returning to the England side to face the All Blacks this weekend. As England seek to clinch back-to-back victories over New Zealand for the first time since 2003, Borthwick has named the same side that beat Australia, barring Will Joseph’s selection in the absence of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

As reported by the Guardian, Borthwick has rewarded Joseph after the 24-year-old scored five tries on his first Twickenham start last time out. The Gloucester flyer switches to the left wing with Tommy Freeman coming back on to the right, meaning he will go head-to-head with New Zealand’s all-time try-scorer Will
title: England and New Zealand bring back big guns in wholesale changes for Twickenham clash

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Party wins biggest majority since Obama and one unthinkable two years ago – now the hard work of investigating and lawmaking begins

It’s official: when Democrats take control of the Senate next year, they’ll have 56 seats, their largest majority in nearly two decades and one that appeared unthinkable at the outset of Donald Trump’s return to power two years ago.

The landslide victory was confirmed on Tuesday, when the lengthy ballot-counting process in Alaska ended with Democrat Mary Peltola defeating the incumbent Dan Sullivan, who became the ninth Republican to see their seat taken by the opposition in a midterm election that produced a political earthquake.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A new day in the Senate’: 56-seat majority gives Democrats fuel to take on Trump

author: Steve Cohen and Michael Shank
description:
Anti-democratic behaviors won’t disappear overnight. The new Congress – and all of us – must rise to the occasion

Americans just witnessed a blue tsunami in the midterm elections, with historic firsts across many US states: the country’s first female Black governor, first female Native American governor, first Muslim US senator, and more.

And while the voters’ repudiation of Donald Trump’s agenda is clear, as Democrats seize the majority of both chambers of Congress, the work to defend our institutions from further democratic backsliding won’t ease up overnight.

Continue reading...
title: After a blue wave, Trump will dig in his heels. We must be more vigilant than ever | Steve Cohen and Michael Shank

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Human rights committee publishes guidance on freedom of association, which criticises vague laws targeting ‘extremism’

The UN human rights committee has warned against the misuse of counter-terrorism and national security legislation as the UK’s highest court considers the lawfulness of the ban on Palestine Action.

In its first comprehensive guidance on freedom of association, the committee criticises vaguely worded laws targeting “extremism” or “undesirable” organisations.

Continue reading...
title: UN warns against misuse of security laws as UK weighs Palestine Action ban

author: Natricia Duncan and Morgan Ofori
description:
Similar processes in South Africa and Rwanda have allowed people to ‘work through’ and heal from their generational trauma

  • Andy Burnham open to calls for formal apology for Britain’s role in slave trade

The UK has agreed to structured dialogue with Commonwealth leaders after the Britsh prime minister, Andy Burnham, indicated he would be open to making a formal apology for Britain’s involvement in the transatlantic slave trade. What would an apology look like in practice and what makes for a meaningful one?
title: Will Britain finally apologise for its role in the slave trade – and why is it so important?

author: Sid Lowe
description:
Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham

The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under-21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her
title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Latest report also says test and trace failures allowed virus to spread quickly and unchecked

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The lack of international border controls at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic left the UK in an “extremely vulnerable position”, an inquiry has concluded.

In the latest report from the Covid-19 inquiry, the chair, Heather Hallett, also said failures to quickly introduce a test-and-trace system allowed the virus to spread “with deadly speed across the country, virtually unchecked”.

Continue reading...
title: Lack of early border controls made UK ‘extremely vulnerable’ to Covid, inquiry finds

author: Guardian Staff
description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

Continue reading...
title: Floods in Florida and blackouts in Kyiv: photos of the day – Thursday

author: Michelle R Smith
description:
Children’s Health Defense, which was allowed back after misinformation ban, accuses tech company of censorship

An anti-vaccine group led for years by Robert F Kennedy Jr said Meta has “taken down” posts on its accounts, after a Guardian report found the group was sharing false and misleading information about vaccines.

The Guardian reported on Wednesday that Children’s Health Defense (CHD) had earlier this year been allowed back on Facebook and Instagram, four years after Meta removed it from Facebook and Instagram for repeatedly violating its misinformation policies.

Continue reading...
title: Anti-vaccine group once led by RFK Jr says Meta removed posts after Guardian report

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Flanagan will become the first Native American woman to serve in the Senate, and hopes young Native people see themselves in her win

Peggy Flanagan, the incoming progressive US senator from Minnesota who claimed her seat after polls showed her in two tight races that she went on to win by double digits, says she has been “underestimated my entire life”.

She was supposedly in a close race during a primary against congresswoman Angie Craig earlier this year. Flanagan, the state’s lieutenant governor with roots in community organizing, won by nearly 20 points.

Continue reading...
title: Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan on her road to victory in Minnesota: ‘I have been underestimated my entire life’

author: Alexis Petridis
description:
(Warp)
The Milan producer revisits his youth as a straight-edge punk fan voyeuristically dabbling in rave – and finds a thrilling interzone between both genres

The opening line of the biography on Lorenzo Senni’s Bandcamp page is striking. “Lorenzo Senni was never a raver,” it reads, something of a blunt admission from a dance producer, or at least a producer who works in an area of electronica influenced by dance music: one might reasonably assume you need some first-hand experience of the dancefloor’s ineffable freedom in order to make music for it. But the Milan-based Senni has made a USP out of his arm’s length distance from what that Bandcamp bio calls a “neon-hued chemical world”.

A straight-edge punk fan in the late 90s, he accompanied friends to Rimini’s hardcore and gabber clubs as a kind of anthropological exercise, a self-styled “rave voyeur” who “just liked to observe and analyse my surroundings”. Accordingly, his albums to date have deal
title: Trance, prog synths, guttural screaming: Lorenzo Senni’s All Ages is the year’s wildest electronic album

author: Ali Martin in Melbourne
description:
Supporters overwhelmingly wanting the captain out over the sandpaper saga which shows no sign of abating

As various protagonists in the sandpaper saga passed through Hobart airport on Thursday – Cricket Australia’s besuited Todd Greenberg with phone in hand pulling a trolley suitcase, a dressed-down Darren Lehmann with a backpack, a Coke, and a thousand-yard stare – there was activity up in Sydney too.

Emerging from the front door of his house and heading off to train with his New South Wales teammates, Pat Cummins was met by a gaggle of local television news reporters who were shouting various things in the hope that Australia’s Test captain might throw some fresh material back.

Continue reading...
title: An outsider’s view of Australian cricket’s civil war: conflicting ‘truths’ and Cummins in a corner | Ali Martin

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
CEO of Cambridge-based firm viewed as leading contender to replace co-founder Jensen Huang according to reports

  • Business live – latest updates

Nvidia’s headhunters have reportedly approached the chief executive of the Cambridge-based chip company Arm, in its search for a new leader after Jensen Huang’s dramatic exit.

Heidrick & Struggles, the recruiting firm hired by the company’s board, has started contacting potential candidates, according to Bloomberg.

Continue reading...
title: Nvidia approaches Arm boss Rene Haas in search for new CEO

author: Kaamil Ahmed in the Hague, and Oliver Holmes
description:
Judgment ends seven-year legal battle and is seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of all state crimes

Myanmar committed acts of genocide against its Rohingya minority during “clearance operations” nearly a decade ago, the world’s highest court has ruled.

The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle and is seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

Continue reading...
title: Myanmar committed acts of genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules

author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
description:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

Continue reading...
title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

author: Hosted by Kai Wright , produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
description: It has been a wild few weeks in the world of tech. First, Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, forced an unimaginable leadership change at Nvidia – arguably the most consequential company in AI development. Then, chaos erupted as a rolling set of IT outages disrupted flights, banking, tech companies and the federal government. And now, Anthropic is blowing minds with a trillion-dollar IPO – one of the largest in stock market history. The Atlantic’s tech writer Charlie Warzel tells Kai Wright that these events are linked: they’re all examples of the ways in which we shoulder unprecedented risk today, in order to bet on AI’s future reward. It’s a convoluted logic that keeps the AI race speeding forward, no matter how many warning signs it blows past. Charlie Warzel is also host of the Atlantic’s podcast Galaxy Brain.
title: Outages, spies, and trillion-dollar IPOs: is this our AI future? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights

More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an open letter published on Thursday.

“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.

Continue reading...
title: Labor leaders call on governments to stop awarding Amazon public contracts

author: Judith Levine
description:
He is responsible for the health of the American people. On his watch, thousands have become seriously ill

At least 11 Americans have died of measles since January 2025 – the month before Robert F Kennedy Jr became secretary of Health and Human Services.

One of Friday’s victims was a child, in Wisconsin, where a baby died of measles the week before. Pennsylvania has not disclosed the age of the other person.

Continue reading...
title: Measles has come raging back in the US. Robert F Kennedy Jr should be impeached | Judith Levine

author: Martin Pengelly
description:
The late director worked with David Hoffman and Dick Russell on a book about his lifelong fascination with what really happened on 22 November 1963

On 8 December last year, the great director Rob Reiner signed off the prologue for Who Killed JFK?, his book written with David Hoffman and Dick Russell and based on his podcast with Soledad O’Brien. Describing a lifelong fascination with the assassination of John F Kennedy in Dallas on 22 November 1963, and what he saw as the vast conspiracy to cover up who really killed the 35th president, Reiner wrote: “Maybe, peop
title: ‘Perhaps we are safer not knowing’: a year after his death, Rob Reiner’s JFK assassination book is revealed

author: Margaret Sullivan
description:
In normal times, we’d expect serious answers from our leaders on a topic of this magnitude. Not under this administration

As outages and disruptions have piled up over recent days, Americans have been searching for answers.

In less than a week, Microsoft went down, the FAA grounded all flights, banking systems were roiled, and the National Security Agency’s internal network failed.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says the tech outages are ‘fine’. Who believes him? | Margaret Sullivan

author: Keza MacDonald
description:
There’s a vast amount to absorb in Leonida, but these pointers will rev up your criminal engines and allow you to better enjoy the ride

Leonida is so huge as to be overwhelming and in the opening hours, the game bombards you with tonnes of info that you will inevitably forget. But I’ve done nothing but play this game for weeks and I’m here to help. Here’s what I wished I’d known at the start

Walk faster. I found that Jason and Lucia walk incredibly slowly. If you go into the options menu, you can select “fast walk” as the default walking speed, which sped them up just a little without ruining the pace or atmosphere of the game. While you’re in there, you can also customise plenty of other things, including controls and button mapping.

Continue reading...
title: Bank your stolen cash, bring a change of clothes, go easy on the bloodshed: 15 tips for playing Grand Theft Auto VI

author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
description:
Running for more than four weeks, 2027 festival features staging of play starring Ewan McGregor and Alan Cumming

The Edinburgh international festival is to stage its longest season next year when it marks 80 years since its foundation in the aftermath of the second world war.

The festival will run for just over four weeks in August 2027, longer than its customary three weeks, and focus heavily on the role of the arts in unifying cultures and transcending conflict.

Continue reading...
title: Edinburgh festival to mark 80-year anniversary with longest ever season

author: Ali Martin in Melbourne
description:
• Root, Duckett, Archer, Atkinson and Baker head home

  • McCullum: ‘Brook has an unbelievable tactical brain’

Fresh from turning over Australia in the 50-over leg of this tour, England’s attention now turns to the Twenty20s that start on Saturday. Five players jet home for a swift breather before the Tests in South Africa, with fresh-faced rookies coming in.

Joe Root, Ben Duckett, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker were the men heading for the departure lounge, while captain Harry Brook and wicketkeeper Jordan Cox will leave after the fourth of the five T20Is on 29 November.

Continue reading...
title: England’s ‘fresh’ rookies roll on to Australia T20s as Test stars depart early

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
Nathan Fielder’s intense close-range study of fraudster Elizabeth Holmes is as gripping as any thriller and much more unhinged

• This review contains spoilers

Thrillingly reckless, deliciously irresponsible and as gripping as any thriller, this situationist docu-hybrid masterpiece from co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim gets up close and personal with convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes. It was Holmes’s US biotech firm Theranos, run jointly with her then partner Sunny Balwani, which in 2003 notoriously claimed to have invented a little box that could diagnose all manner of illnesses from a single drop of blood, its corporate prestige pumped by credulous board members including George Schultz and Henry
title: You Can See Everything review – unblinking, unhinged and unmissable

author: Jared Beasley
description:
A professional sports career does not guarantee wealth. And a growing number of athletes are turning to alternative streams of income

“I’m sick and tired of it.” Bart Swings tossed his jacket behind him. It was August 2025, the Winter Olympics were less than six months away, and the Belgian Olympic champion’s injured knee was not getting better. The clip, profanity and all, later ran on the Belgian evening news along with the weather and the football. But the injury update didn’t come from an interview – it was broadcast on the speed skater’s OnlyFans channel.

The subscription site, best known for porn dudes, cam girls and dubiously horny couples, has quietly assembled one of the stranger rosters in professional sport. The list, about 285 athletes deep, includes Olympic speed skaters and rowers, tennis players, surfers and golfers. And, despite its racy reputation, many of the athletes on OnlyFans are not putting out adult content.
title: From training clips to thirst traps: why athletes are turning to OnlyFans

author: Peter Muiruri
description:
Families of journalists who vanished into state prisons on ‘Black Tuesday’ in 2001 do not know whether they are even still alive

When Fisseha Yirgalem stepped on to the podium and began reading from a letter written to a man who may never hear it, the room full of journalists in Nairobi fell quiet.

The Eritrean writer’s personal tribute to Amanuel Asrat, a poet, writer, and founder of Zemen newspaper, was not merely about an abstract human rights case but about her mentor, former colleague and friend whose life had in effect been erased by the authoritarian state of Eritrea.

Continue reading...
title: Mentors, colleagues and friends: tributes paid to the ‘Eritrea 16’ who disappeared 25 years ago

author: Owen Myers
description:
In Madonna Into the Groove: An Intimate Portrait of the Queen of Pop, photographer Ken Regan opens his archive from 1985 to show never-before-seen photographs of the musician. The 160-page hardback showcases Madonna at her most vibrant, captured on a February day in Los Angeles, with accompanying biographical text by journalist Tomás Mier. With the majority of images previously unpublished, the book is a behind-the-scenes look at an artist coming into the peak of her powers

Continue reading...
title: ‘No publicist or manager in sight’: 80s Madonna, unseen and off-duty – in pictures

author: Guardian Staff
description:
After US president called Putin a friend, Poland’s PM said: ‘God, protect us from such friends’

On Ukraine, Trump says at the beginning of the trilateral meeting:

“We are going to be discussing the war between Russia and Ukraine, and we already have. President Putin and I have had a long discussion today for quite a while. That’s what pretty much what the discussion was about.

And I think things are happening.

Continue reading...
title: Tusk appears to mock Trump’s Putin comment as Ukraine’s allies meet in Berlin – Europe live

author: Emma Joyce
description:
The Brisbane musician shared earlier this year that he was ‘entering the final chapter of my life’ as chemotherapy had been unable to stop the cancer from spreading

The Bugs bassist Jordan Brunoli has died aged 31, a year after being diagnosed with terminal colorectal cancer.

The Brisbane musician first shared his diagnosis with stage-four cancer in June 2025 after undergoing surgery to remove tumours from his bowel and lymph nodes.

Continue reading...
title: Bugs bassist Jordan Brunoli dies aged 31, one year after cancer diagnosis

author: Tom McIlroy in Shenzhen
description:
Australian prime minister uses speech at Apec summit in China to call for Russian president to end five-year war

The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has urged Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine, using a speech at the Apec summit in China to call out the Russian president.

Speaking at the Asian Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) talks in Shenzhen, Albanese looked directly at Putin during the comments.

Continue reading...
title: ‘End your war, end it now’: Anthony Albanese tells Vladimir Putin to put a stop to Ukraine war

author: Tumaini Carayol
description:
British tennis star has bounced back after six months out but wants more to be done about vitriol aimed at players

Sonay Kartal believes the vitriolic abuse and threats that she and her fellow players receive after every match have become an unavoidable part of her job.

“Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” the British No 2 says. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I see comments every day’: Sonay Kartal’s fightback against injury and online abuse

author: Sian Cain
description:
Assadi’s third novel was inspired by the story of her late father, a Palestinian who escaped the Nakba as a child in 1948

Palestinian-Jewish author Hannah Lillith Assadi has won the National book award for fiction, one of the US’s most prestigious literary prizes, for her novel Paradiso 17.

Assadi’s third novel is a study of the psychic toll of displacement on migrants, through the tale of a Palestinian man who escaped the Nakba in 1948, when more than 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes by Israel. The story was inspired by her father, Sami Abdul-Fattah Al-Assadi, who fled the Nakba as a child with his family, before studying in Italy and moving to New York.

Continue reading...
title: Hannah Lillith Assadi wins National book award for ‘visionary’ novel Paradiso 17

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Exclusive: Industry tactics are part of ‘deliberate strategy’ to distort evidence and weaken regulation, paper says

Prof Charlotta Pisinger, a medical doctor and public health researcher, was speaking to this journalist about her experiences of intimidation by the tobacco industry when another complaint to her employer landed in her inbox.

The Danish subsidiary of the tobacco company Philip Morris International (PMI) had just filed a complaint accusing her of breaching the University of Southern Denmark’s research communication standards for media interviews she gave questioning the safety of heated tobacco and vapes and whether PMI really cared about improving health.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The abuse I copped was phenomenal’: researchers accuse tobacco companies of intimidation tactics to silence critics

author: Sarah Johnson
description:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world has no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Chataigniers en fleurs (Chestnut Trees in Blossom), which was painted in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, France, set a new record for the Dutch post-impressionist

A Vincent van Gogh masterpiece sold for a record-breaking $190.4m (£144.9m, A$285m) on Wednesday after a dispute between the seller and the heirs of a previous Jewish owner who sold it in the Nazi era, Sotheby’s said.

Chataigniers en fleurs (Chestnut Trees in Blossom), which was painted in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, France, set a new record for the Dutch post-impressionist and became the most expensive work auctioned off so far this season.

Continue reading...
title: Vincent van Gogh painting auctioned for record $190.4m after dispute over Nazi era sale

author: Lucy Campbell and Robert Mackey
description:
Musk, who aligned with Trump and was frequent White House guest, says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ about record midterm spending

Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intensely with Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement since 2024.

“I’m not Maga,” the world’s richest person told the New York Times Dealbook summit, which he attended via video call from China, where he is one of several US business leaders who have accompanied Trump on his trip to Asia.

Continue reading...
title: Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not Maga’ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans
